rubric.why: Identifies the main purpose of U-235.
rubric.description: States that U-235 is used as a nuclear fuel.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying its use as fuel.

rubric.why: Links the use of U-235 to the production of useful energy.
rubric.description: States that energy released in a reactor is used to generate electricity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking its use in a reactor or its fission to electricity generation.

modelAnswer: Uranium-235 is used as a nuclear fuel in reactors.
Energy released by its fission is used to generate electricity.

items.followUp: Explain why oil does not dissolve readily in water.

rubric.why: Explains the principle in terms of the similar polarity of solute and solvent.
rubric.description: States that polar solutes dissolve in polar solvents and nonpolar solutes dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating either or both polarity relationships.

rubric.why: A suitable example demonstrates the principle.
rubric.description: Gives an example such as sodium chloride dissolving in water, or oil not dissolving readily in water.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid example that applies the principle.

modelAnswer: “Like dissolves like” means polar solutes dissolve in polar solvents, while nonpolar solutes dissolve in nonpolar solvents.
For example, sodium chloride dissolves in polar water, whereas nonpolar oil does not dissolve readily in water.
